name: NetExec
what: A network execution toolkit (command `nxc`) that talks SMB, LDAP, WinRM, MSSQL, RDP, SSH and more so you can validate credentials, run modules and move through a Windows domain during an authorized internal assessment. It is the actively maintained successor to CrackMapExec.
when: After you have written scope and a lab or production approval, when you need to spray or verify domain credentials, enumerate shares, dump secrets with an approved module, or confirm which hosts accept a given account.
example: Install on an approved assessment host: `pipx install git+https://github.com/Pennyw0rth/NetExec`.
Confirm SMB reachability for an in-scope subnet: `nxc smb 10.10.20.0/24`.
Test a service account against that range only: `nxc smb 10.10.20.0/24 -u svc_backup -p 'REDACTED'`.
Run a single agreed module (for example share listing) and export results for the report; do not enable destructive modules without a change ticket.
Hand findings to the blue team with host, account and module name so detections can be tuned.
pitfalls: Credential spraying and secret-dump modules can lock accounts or trip EDR; agree lockout thresholds and SOC notification first.
CrackMapExec is archived; use NetExec, not the old packages.
Keep captured hashes and tickets in the engagement vault and wipe them when the report is delivered.
